_comment: Settings of the weekly build (build/weekly.py). 'states' is the one list to change: add "oh" to build and publish Ohio too (its routing then joins Pennsylvania's in one graph, as the app needs for two states on one phone).

ca.name: California
ca._addresses_note: as Ohio (no NAD step); first built in the California trial (beamline docs/next-round.md item 48)

oh.name: Ohio
oh._addresses_note: no NAD step: the hosted NAD service needs about 9 hours for Ohio (more than one job may run); OSM points and TIGER ranges only, as in round 3

extract_fallback._comment: When a state's <state>-latest.osm.pbf cannot be downloaded (after the retries) or never matches its .md5, the newest dated extract <state>-YYMMDD.osm.pbf of the same Geofabrik folder that downloads and matches its own .md5 is used, if the map date in its header is at most max_age_days old. The log and run.json ('extracts') say which file was used and why.

comma._comment: Every comma step (Mapd's setup, the three comma files of each state, their check, comma.json) runs in a process group of its own; past step_time_limit_s the whole group is killed and the step counts as failed, so a stalled git fetch or Go module download cannot use up the job's 345 minutes and hold back the phone's packs. A whole run took 46 minutes on 2026-11-22.

shrink_check._comment: A new build fails when its pack is much smaller than the published one of the same state (a broken input). Ratios of this week's bytes to last week's.

search_check._comment: packbuilder/search/tests/run_tests.py on the pack's own search and address files. top5 = share of cases with the expected result in the first five; 'excl_gaps' leaves out the cases the data cannot answer.

route_check._comment: build/check_routes.py: each trip must route on the pack's own routing part, with its length within the tolerance of the reference and both ends within max_end_gap_m of a road.

inputs._comment: The slower-changing inputs, kept between weekly runs in the release tagged 'inputs' (see README). policy: pinned = fetched once (the builders pin them by version or SHA-256) and reused; upstream = fetched again when the publisher has a newer file and the kept copy is at least min_age_days old; max_age = fetched again when the kept copy is older than max_age_days (the kept copy is used if that fails). A 'dir' item travels as one tar.
